market_pricing_in:
At current market levels of $105.55 per share (trading at 13.2x P/OE and 11.9x EV/OE), Mr. Market is pricing in a pronounced growth deceleration and structural margin compression for Kaspi.kz. The market's primary concern centers on domestic saturation in Kazakhstan, where user engagement has peaked at an impressive 77 transactions per month per active consumer across 14 million monthly active users (MAU). Furthermore, Payments segment take rates compressed 7 basis points year-over-year to 1.00%, causing Payments Adjusted EBITDA to decline 1% YoY and stalling consolidated net income growth (+0% YoY in Q2 2026 at ₸259 billion) despite top-line revenue expansion of 15% YoY ($2.3B).

Compounding these operational headwinds is significant geopolitical, regulatory, and capital allocation skepticism. Investors continue to apply an emerging market and secondary sanctions discount following short-seller allegations from Culper Research regarding Russian non-resident accounts and correspondent banking links, alongside elevated credit provisions (+25.5% YoY in early 2026) and surging deposit funding costs (~14.3%). Additionally, Kaspi's cross-border expansion into Turkey via the $1.13 billion acquisition of Hepsiburada and $300 million capital commitment to Hepsi Bank introduces hyperinflationary accounting (IAS 29), lira currency depreciation, and near-term margin dilution, leading the market to treat current earnings as cyclical peak.
why_it_might_be_right:
1. Starting Baseline: State starting normalized Owner Earnings of $8.00/share ($8.0M total, subtracting $3.0M in stock-based compensation and $4.0M in maintenance CapEx) and net balance sheet cash of $+10.00/share ($+10.0M total).

2. Forensic Business Headwinds: If skeptic warnings materialize, Kaspi faces severe structural margin degradation. Take-rate erosion in Payments accelerates below 0.90% due to local competition and merchant pushback, while domestic deposit rates remain elevated at 14%+, permanently compressing Fintech net interest margins. Concurrently, secondary sanctions fallout or regulatory enforcement severely restricts cross-border flows, while integration costs and Lira depreciation at Hepsiburada in Turkey absorb cash without yielding accretive earnings.

3. Skeptic Unit Contraction: Under this bear case, active commercial volume units contract by 12% as merchant churn increases and consumer purchasing power diminishes under inflation. Total Payment Value (TPV) contracts, loan origination volumes shrink due to tighter credit underwriting, and expected credit loss (ECL) provisions spike 40% to cover rising non-performing consumer loans.

4. Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation: Fixed platform operating overhead, regulatory compliance costs, and sticky server/network expenses resist rapid downsizing. Degraded revenues combined with higher funding costs and credit losses compress Owner Cash Margins, reducing normalized Owner Earnings to $4.00 per share ($4.0M total).

5. Downside Risk Valuation Floor: Capitalizing degraded Owner Earnings of $4.00/share at a conservative trough multiple of 5.0x P/OE (reflecting Narrow Moat distress and heightened geopolitical/regulatory risk) yields $20.00/share in business value. Adding depleted net balance sheet cash of $8.00/share yields a Downside Floor Target of $28.00/share.
how_things_are_going_now:
Despite narrative skepticism, Kaspi's operational engine maintains solid top-line momentum, generating an annualized revenue run-rate of $1,000.0M across its tri-engine Super-App. In Q2 2026, Marketplace GMV grew 15% YoY to $4.8B (with core e-commerce GMV up 28% YoY constant currency), while Fintech revenues surged 23% YoY to $946M on an 18% expansion in the average net loan portfolio ($15.2B). Engagement among its 14 million MAU remains unmatched globally, averaging 77 transactions per consumer per month.

However, operational reality highlights clear margin friction. Payments segment revenue grew just 5% YoY to $351M as take rates compressed to 1.00%, causing Payments Adjusted EBITDA to edge down 1% YoY to $204M. Surging interest expenses from 14.3% retail deposit rates limited Q2 2026 Net Income growth to +0% YoY (₸259B / $539M). Management is actively mitigating funding costs through recent 100 bps deposit rate cuts, rolling out "Kasper" AI conversion tools, and scaling Hepsi Bank in Turkey to establish a multi-country growth engine.
what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
1. Starting Unit Baseline: Exact starting baseline anchored at Active commercial volume units, generating an annualized revenue run-rate of $1,000.0M, normalized Owner Earnings of $8.00/share ($8.0M total), and net balance sheet cash of $+10.00/share ($+10.0M total).

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Over the 3-year visible runway, active commercial volume units expand steadily at ~5.0% per annum (Year 1: 1.05x, Year 2: 1.10x, Year 3: 1.16x baseline), driven by continuous cross-selling across Payments, Marketplace, and Fintech, alongside early contributions from Turkish e-commerce order volume.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue: Multiplying Year 3 volume units (1.16x baseline) by stabilized unit monetization yield (reflecting deposit rate easing in late 2026/2027 offsetting minor Payments take-rate pressure) generates Projected Year 3 Revenue of $1,200.0M (representing a disciplined ~6.3% CAGR).

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Subtracting cash fixed operating overhead, funding costs, maintenance CapEx ($5.0M), and stock-based compensation ($3.5M) from $1,200.0M revenue results in Projected Year 3 Total Owner Earnings of $11.0M ($11.00/share), representing an Owner Cash Margin of 0.92% on gross platform flows and an underlying Year 3 YoY OE growth rate (g₃) of 12.2% YoY ($11.0M vs $9.8M in Year 2).

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Starting Net Cash ($10.0M) + Cumulative 3-Year FCF generated ($28.5M) - Growth CapEx/M&A commitments ($6.0M) - Share Repurchases & Dividends ($18.0M) = Ending Year 3 Net Cash of $14.5M ($14.50/share).

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: With Year 3 Owner Earnings growth g₃ at 12.2% YoY, the 2-Factor Exit Multiple Matrix for a Narrow Moat Steady Compounding business specifies a multiple range of 12.0x–15.0x P/OE. Applying a disciplined 13.5x P/OE multiple to Year 3 OE of $11.00/share yields a capitalized earnings value of $148.50/share. Adding Ending Net Cash of $14.50/share delivers an Intrinsic Fair Value Target of $163.00/share. From today's market price of $105.55, this implies a 3-Year Expected Annualized Return (IRR) of 15.6% per annum.

What the Market is Pricing In

At current market levels of $105.55 per share (trading at 13.2x P/OE and 11.9x EV/OE), Mr. Market is pricing in a pronounced growth deceleration and structural margin compression for Kaspi.kz. The market's primary concern centers on domestic saturation in Kazakhstan, where user engagement has peaked at an impressive 77 transactions per month per active consumer across 14 million monthly active users (MAU). Compounding these operational headwinds is significant geopolitical, regulatory, and capital allocation skepticism. Investors continue to apply an emerging market and secondary sanctions discount following short-seller allegations from Culper Research regarding Russian non-resident accounts and correspondent banking links, alongside elevated credit provisions (+25.5% YoY in early 2026) and surging deposit funding costs (~14.3%).
